title: N-1 and N-2 (Japanese) domains
statement: Let $R$ be an integral domain with field of fractions $K$. (1) $R$ is *N-1* if the integral closure of $R$ in $K$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. (2) $R$ is *N-2*, or *Japanese*, if for every finite field extension $L/K$ [def-pc-field-extension] (i.e. $\dim_KL<\infty$) the integral closure of $R$ in $L$, where $L$ is an $R$-algebra through the composite $R\subseteq K\to L$, is a finitely generated $R$-module. Taking $L=K$ shows that an N-2 domain is N-1.

proof.text: For isN1_of_isN2, specialize the IsN2 R K hypothesis to L = K. The self-algebra K/K, the compatible scalar tower R/K/K, and finite dimensionality of K over itself are Mathlib instances. The resulting Module.Finite R (integralClosure R K) is definitionally IsN1 R K.

proof_origin: Stacks Project, Algebra, Definition 10.161.1 (Tag 032F): the trivial finite extension L = K gives N-1 from N-2; implemented by definitional specialization h K.
